This example demonstrates the `quarto-notes-filter` extension across the
four supported output formats. Render it with any of:

```bash
quarto render example.qmd --to html
quarto render example.qmd --to pdf
quarto render example.qmd --to typst
quarto render example.qmd --to docx
```

## Basic usage {#sec-basic}

Add a `fig-notes` attribute to any figure and an AER-style "Notes:" line
is rendered below the caption. The source for @fig-elephant below is:

```markdown
![A caption goes here.](elephant.png){#fig-elephant
  fig-notes="Figure produced following the literate-programming approach
  of @knuth1984 and typeset with @lamport1994. The shaded area is
  illustrative."
  width=60%}
```

which renders as:

![A caption goes here.](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/elephant.png){#fig-elephant
  fig-notes="Figure produced following the literate-programming approach of @knuth1984 and typeset with @lamport1994. The shaded area is illustrative."
  width=60%}

See @fig-elephant.

## Cross-references and citations work inside notes {#sec-refs}

The `fig-notes` content is parsed as Markdown and runs through Quarto's
usual citeproc + crossref pipeline, so you can use `@sec-x`, `@fig-x`,
and `@cite-key` inside notes just like in regular text:

```markdown
![A second figure.](elephant.png){#fig-elephant2
  fig-notes="Replication of @fig-elephant from @sec-basic, following
  @knuth1984. See @sec-options for available options."
  width=60%}
```

![A second figure.](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/elephant.png){#fig-elephant2
  fig-notes="Replication of @fig-elephant from @sec-basic, following @knuth1984. See @sec-options for available options."
  width=60%}

## Custom title and scale {#sec-options}

Per-figure overrides via `fig-notes-title` and `fig-notes-scale`:

```markdown
![Another figure.](elephant.png){#fig-elephant3
  fig-cap="Another figure."
  fig-notes="Sample of 1,234 observations."
  fig-notes-title="Source:"
  fig-notes-scale=0.8
  width=60%}
```

![Another figure.](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/elephant.png){#fig-elephant3
  fig-cap="Another figure."
  fig-notes="Sample of 1,234 observations."
  fig-notes-title="Source:"
  fig-notes-scale=0.8
  width=60%}

Document-wide defaults can also be set in YAML front matter:

```yaml
fig-notes-title: "Notes:"
fig-notes-scale: 0.9
tbl-notes-title: "Notes:"
tbl-notes-scale: 0.9
```

## Working with Code

````markdown
```{.r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "A scatter plot."
#| fig-notes: "This figure demonstrates a scatter plot."
#| echo: false
plot(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$hp)
```
````

```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "A scatter plot."
#| fig-notes: "This figure demonstrates a scatter plot."
#| echo: false
plot(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$hp)
```


## Table notes {#sec-tables}

The same attribute is available for Markdown tables as `tbl-notes`, which
mirrors the `notes` option of the `tinytable` package: the note is
rendered as the final row of the table itself, flush against the bottom
rule.

```markdown
| fruit  | price  |
|--------|--------|
| apple  | 2.05   |
| pear   | 1.37   |
| orange | 3.09   |

: Fruit prices. {#tbl-fruit
  tbl-notes="Prices follow the conventions of @knuth1984. See
  @sec-basic for the corresponding figure."}
```

| fruit  | price  |
|--------|--------|
| apple  | 2.05   |
| pear   | 1.37   |
| orange | 3.09   |

: Fruit prices. {#tbl-fruit tbl-notes="Prices follow the conventions of @knuth1984. See @sec-basic for the corresponding figure."}

See @tbl-fruit. Per-table `tbl-notes-title` and `tbl-notes-scale`
overrides work just like the figure variants:

| Col1 | Col2 | Col3 |
|------|------|------|
| A    | B    | C    |
| E    | F    | G    |
| A    | G    | G    |

: My caption. {#tbl-letters
  tbl-notes="Reproduced from @lamport1994. See @sec-options."
  tbl-notes-title="Source:"
  tbl-notes-scale=0.8}
